If the figure above shows the graph of $g(x),$ then

${lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{g(x)}{{x}^{2}}=$
 {{field-1}}.

current_example.worked_solution:
First, we use the algebra of limits to pull out the constant factor of $\dfrac 1 4\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{1}{4{x}^{4}} & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{4}} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot {lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{1}{{x}^{4}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the fact that

$$
\lim_\limits{x \to \infty} \left(\dfrac{1}{x^4}\right)=0,
$$

we can evaluate our limit as follows:

$$
\dfrac{1}{4} \cdot\lim_\limits{x \to \infty} \dfrac{1}{x^4} = \dfrac 1 4\cdot 0 = 0
$$
